newsitem.title: USA: Chernomyrdin briefs Clinton on Yeltsin surgery.
newsitem.headline: Chernomyrdin briefs Clinton on Yeltsin surgery.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin telephoned President Bill Clinton on Tuesday and told him President Boris Yeltsin's heart surgery had been successful, the White House said.

Chernomyrdin telephoned Clinton here at 11:20 a.m. CDT (1720 GMT) on U.S. election day to report on the success of the operation, performed earlier on Tuesday, White House spokesman Mike McCurry said, adding that the conversation was brief.

McCurry said Clinton sent a government-to-government message to the Kremlin expressing U.S. hopes for Yeltsin's speedy recovery. Clinton and his wife Hillary sent a separate message to Yeltsin and his wife Naina conveying their best personal wishes, he said.
In Washington, Defence Department spokesman Ken Bacon said the United States was not concerned about the security of Russia's nuclear weapons stockpile while the operation was under way.
Bacon said: "We believe that adequate steps were taken to oversee and command the nuclear arsenal by turning over government authority to Prime Minister Chernomyrdin."
The State Department said Washington was pleased Yeltsin's heart operation appeared to go well and officials said they hoped to get a private briefing from one of Yeltsin's doctors.
"The United States is very pleased that President Yeltsin's operation appears to have gone well and we wish him the best for a speedy and full recovery," spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.
"We look forward to the day when he can resume fully his responsibilities as president of Russia," he said.
During Yeltsin's convalescence, Chernomyrdin will hold the reins of power. Burns said "we have an excellent relationship with Prime Minister Chernomyrdin and have full confidence in him."
Officials said they were trying to get a private briefing on Yeltsin's condition from Dr. Michael DeBakey, the pioneering American surgeon who was an observer in Yeltsin's case.
Yeltsin came through seven hours of open heart surgery but it will be some time before Russians will know if the 65-year-old president can return to full health.
"The operation was a complete success," said DeBakey, 88, in Moscow.
